subject: Saltwood service impact: proposed credit & remediation plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@saltwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@saltwood.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected latency & errors on inference endpoints (Oct 27 22:00 - Oct 28 03:30 UTC)

Hi Tessa,

We saw a significant regression in inference latency and a spike in 5xx errors across our production routes overnight. Impact window appears to be ~22:00 UTC on Oct 27 through ~03:30 UTC Oct 28. During the worst period our p95 latency rose to ~1.1s from ~240ms baseline and we observed throughput drops of ~35% on our high-priority routes. Several of our downstream jobs aborted due to repeated 5xxs (error rate peaked ~4.8%).

This incident caused multiple customer-facing failures for Saltwood and we need to understand next steps: immediate mitigation you can apply, proposed compensatory credits for SLA breach, and a timeline for a technical root-cause and permanent mitigation. We have a renewal conversation in 6 weeks and need a firm plan.

Please escalate to your ops and sales leadership.

Best,
Elena
Director of Platform Operations
Saltwood Analytics

Attachments: log-snippet-1028.txt (text), request-id-sample.txt (text)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@saltwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & errors on inference endpoints (Oct 27 22:00 - Oct 28 03:30 UTC)

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and sorry for the impact. We have our on-call engineers investigating now. Initial signals point to a degraded autoscaling reaction on a subset of Dedicated nodes serving your tenant which led to queueing and elevated request failures.

Immediate plan:
- We’ve increased burst capacity for Saltwood to stop further throttling (completed 09:38 PT).
- Bounced the affected pool and applied a hotfix to the scaler logic (09:55 PT).
- We’ve seeded an additional KV-cache warm cluster to reduce cold-start token overhead for your busiest routes.

I’m looping in Sean and Lauren for credits and contractual coordination — we will return with a proposed credit calculation and a draft remediation runbook within 48 hours.

I’ll follow up with a short post-incident note and timeline.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@saltwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed credit & remediation — Saltwood incident Oct 27-28

Elena —

Thanks again for raising this. We reviewed the telemetry and followed your logs; we agree the event constitutes an SLA breach under section 3.2 (availability and error rate). Per contract the baseline remedy is a pro-rated service credit for the impacted billing period.

Proposal (for discussion):
- Credit calculation: we propose a 12% service credit on Nov invoice reflecting the aggregate minutes of degraded service during the event window. The attached sla_credit_calc.xlsx shows the minute-by-minute impact and how we computed the 12% (we used your traffic-weighted routes).
- One-time engineering remediation: priority code review & production hardening of scaler with a 30-day target to reach improved autoscaling SLOs. We will share a remediation runbook and weekly status updates.
- Executive review: our VP of Sales will sign off on any credit above 10% (internal policy). If Saltwood requests more than the proposed 12% we’ll need to route to finance + legal for approval.

We’d like to schedule a 30-minute remediation & credits call with your ops and product leads tomorrow. Proposed times: Oct 30 10:00PT or Oct 30 15:00PT. Which works?

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_credit_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Elena Park <elena.park@saltwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@saltwood.com, martin.stewart@stewartlaw.com
Date: 2026-10-29T12:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed credit & remediation — Saltwood incident Oct 27-28

Sean, Tessa —

Thanks for the quick proposal. We appreciate the prompt mitigation steps. A few notes from Saltwood:
- The proposed 12% looks reasonable as a starting point but it understates downstream business impact. Our procurement and finance team will want visibility into the calculation inputs (you already provided the spreadsheet — thanks).
- Saltwood is requesting an additional make-good: 30,000 free inference units for two weeks to offset lost ops during remediation (this is a discrete consumption credit we can apply to peak routing).
- We’d like SLA language clarified: what guardrails will you include to prevent recurrence (autoscale thresholds, warm pool guarantees, paging escalation)?

I’ve looped in Martin (counsel) as we may need a contract addendum for any change to credits or service guarantees.

Can we confirm the meeting at Oct 30 15:00 PT?

Best,
Elena

Attachments: impact-summary.pdf (PDF)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@saltwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed credit & remediation — Saltwood incident Oct 27-28

Elena / Martin / Saltwood team —

Thank you for the conversation earlier. Quick recap and action items agreed on the call:
1) Credit: Redwood will apply a 12% pro-rated service credit on Saltwood’s November invoice. Finance has pre-approved this amount and will issue the credit without the need for a signed amendment.
2) Consumption make-good: We will grant a one-time 20,000 inference unit consumption credit valid for 30 days (we were able to stretch beyond the initial internal ask). If Saltwood still needs additional units after this allocation, we will accelerate a support arrangement to prioritize routing.
3) Technical guardrails: Engineering will implement three mitigations within 30 days — improved autoscale hysteresis, warm-pool guarantee for the top 5 routes, and a new health-check-triggered emergency scaler. We’ll publish the runbook and weekly progress updates.
4) Exec oversight: Sean will prepare an executive note summarizing commitments; Tessa will coordinate renewal implications.

Open items:
- Saltwood asked for a contract addendum to codify warm-pool guarantees. Legal has to review; until signed, the runbook and credits stand as a commercial commitment.
- Martin requested the detailed minute-level telemetry export; David will deliver that by Nov 1.

Action owners and deadlines:
- David Kim: export telemetry + minute-level impact CSV (due 2026-11-01)
- Redwood eng (owner TBD): publish runbook draft (due 2026-11-12)
- Sean: exec summary for Saltwood leadership (due 2026-11-02)

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (draft)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@saltwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Telemetry export + next steps

Team —

Attached is the minute-level export from our monitoring for the Saltwood tenant covering Oct 27 20:00 UTC through Oct 28 06:00 UTC. Key highlights:
- Total impacted minutes (latency > 500ms or 5xx rate > 1%): 310 minutes
- Peak error rate: 4.8% (2026-10-28T01:17 UTC)
- Average p95 during window: 870ms (weighted across routes)

Per our formula (weighted by route traffic share), the 12% credit in the attached calculation reconciles to the 310 impacted minutes used. If Saltwood prefers to use a different weighting, we can re-run the calc.

Next steps: Sean will circulate the executive note and Lauren will track the runbook publication. Legal: please advise if you need the credit documented in an amendment; otherwise finance will apply the 12% and the 20k unit consumption credit as described.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Observability & Monitoring
Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry-impact-1027-1028.csv (CSV)
